newsitem.title: USA: Brisk U.S. cattle sales may buoy prices - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Brisk U.S. cattle sales may buoy prices - analyst.

text.p: Many U.S. Plains cattle feeders the past two weeks have been marketing cattle ahead of schedule, a trend which could result in slightly higher than expected fed cattle prices this winter, market sources said.

"I'm almost 40 days ahead on marketings," said one Kansas cattle feeder, adding that profitable packer offers and attractive prices on replacement feeders encouraged him and others to be aggressive sellers of slaughter cattle.
Most cattle sold this week at $71 per hundredweight, yielding about $85 to $100 a head profit, analysts said.

Lower corn prices this fall have helped profitability which contributed to the increase in sales of 'green' cattle not yet finished, or fed to the ideal market weights that meat packers prefer for higher grading cuts of beef.
Beef cattle usually are on feed at feedlots for 110 to 130 days before being sold to packers.
The recent accelerated fed cattle marketings could reduce the number of cattle expected to be available in mid-December, Dean Witter livestock analyst Dale Benson said.
"In the next 20 days, prices could range from $69 to $72 but I wouldn't be surprised to see it go higher," he said.
"I'm really having a difficult time estimating the number of marketings we're going to have and the number of cattle that we're going to be putting on the showlists," Benson said.

He said increased placements of cattle into feedlots in August, September and early October had been expected to flood the market with cattle by December 10th or 15th but the recent marketings could instead level off that expected supply bulge.
The Texas Cattle Feeders Association said this past week's showlist of 53,807 head was the smallest since 51,183 were listed the week of January 4, 1993.

Dave Maher, livestock analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa, said cattle prices could come down in another week to 10 days as the current marketing hole starts to close and demand shifts to hams and turkeys for the Thanksgiving holiday.

Maher projected an average fourth quarter price for Texas steers at $68.50, from a projected range of $66 to $71. He pegged monthly average prices at $70.50 in October, $69.50 in November and $67.50 in December.
At the close of trading Thursday, CME December live cattle futures were priced at the equivalent of $66.675 per cwt.
However, weather can make a big difference where prices are, Maher added. "If we have a real rough winter, we can easily put $2 on prices," he said. (Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8720)
